item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Quiet Caption Over The Lake

turns.text: Put “A little room to breathe” over this photo, near the bottom in clean white lettering. Keep the whole wide photo, just add the caption.

item.tests: Tests exact caption rendering, readable placement, and preservation of the supplied photograph.

answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: A little room to breathe — English, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Style and placement: Clean white lettering near the bottom; calm and understated.
answer_sheet.Picture and output size: Use lake.jpg, retain the full 16:9 frame; free-tier image size is fine.

must_haves: The caption reads exactly 'A little room to breathe', without quotation marks.
The caption is white, readable, and placed near the bottom with no clipped letters.
The supplied mountain lake, pine trees, and sky remain recognizable and retain the original full framing.
The caption appears as a graphic overlay, not as a physical object in the scene.

turns.text: Put “A little room to breathe” over this pic, near the bottom in clean white lettering. Keep the whole wide photo, just add the caption. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has been generated, and no credits have been spent.**

For “A little room to breathe” near the bottom in clean white lettering:

- **Cheapest and best fit: 0 Magic Hour credits.** A basic text overlay in a free editor such as Photopea can keep the entire wide photo at its original size and leave the photo itself unchanged.
- **Through Magic Hour:** the lowest listed image-editing price is **from 5 credits** for one image using Flux 2 Klein at **640px**. I can’t verify an exact final charge with the available tools. This is an AI edit, so it may alter details beyond the caption.

**Smaller or shorter?** 640px is the smallest listed AI output option; shortening the caption doesn’t lower the per-image cost.

I recommend the free text-overlay route for this simple change. Would you like quick instructions, or would you prefer the paid-credit AI edit?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the free text-overlay route. Please give me quick instructions for lake.jpg, keeping the full 16:9 frame.

turns.agent:
Use **Photopea** in your browser—no Magic Hour credits needed:

1. Open **photopea.com**, then choose **File → Open** and select `lake.jpg`.
2. **Don’t crop or resize** the image; keep the entire wide frame.
3. Select the **Text tool (T)** and click near the bottom center.
4. Type exactly: **A little room to breathe**
5. Set the text to **white**, using a clean font such as **Arial Regular**. Start around **24 px** for the pictured size and adjust to taste.
6. Center it horizontally, leaving roughly **6–8% of the image height** beneath the lettering. If needed, add a subtle dark shadow for readability.
7. Choose **File → Export As → JPG**, keep the original dimensions, and use **95–100% quality**.

**Aspect-ratio note:** the preview appears slightly taller than 16:9. Keeping the whole image unchanged preserves its existing ratio. If the actual file isn’t 16:9, making it exactly 16:9 requires either cropping or adding borders; use borders if you want to retain every part of the photo.
